evidence: Cic. Brut. 70: jam plānē perfecta (Lewis & Short, s.v. perficiō)
Cic. de Or. 1.59: ōrātōrem plēnum atque perfectum
terms.comment: The participle of perficiō, “carry through, finish”: what has been brought to completion and lacks nothing.

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.14: perfectum atque absolūtum officium (Lewis & Short, s.v. perficiō)
terms.comment: From absolvō, “finish” (of a picture or a book); often paired with perfectus. Pliny’s omnibus numerīs absolūtus is “perfect in every respect” (Morgan–Owens).

terms.gloss: finished to a fingernail, perfectly polished
terms.comment: A craftsman’s image: a joint smooth enough for the fingernail to pass over it without catching (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: perficio · Lewis & Short: absolvo · Lewis & Short: unguis
